candidateSegments.teachingRole: Changing travel direction motivates velocity vector; then isolate constant speed in our model.

observed.action: Car turns through bend while displayed mph decreases, then exits.
observed.result: Heading and path direction change visibly.

claimLimits: Speed is NOT constant:84→103→64→73mph; do not narrate actual footage as uniform circular motion.
Road is irregular, not calibrated circular arc; no measured radius or centripetal acceleration.

annotationPlan.target: Road-following open curve and short travel direction arrow; actual mph readout stays visible.
annotationPlan.style: Progressive open contour/short leader/path with labels. No invented game measurements or internal force/skeleton data.
annotationPlan.tracking: These inspected sample frames are planning evidence, not per-frame tracking. Follow actual target; hide at occlusion/out-of-frame; clear at cut.
annotationPlan.captionClearance: Fixed bottom-centre captions and game UI protected; foreground callout should not cover the action.

candidateSegments.status: Concept observed in native-source temporal frames; full continuous playback, audio and final tracked composite QA pending

candidateSegments.teachingRole: Object rotation around axes rather than movement of a running character.

observed.before: A sail lies beside joined logs.

observed.result: The same mast and crossbar adopt a new orientation.

claimLimits: Discrete manipulation is not constant angular speed.
Use in-game rotation axes only as observed UI; own canonical angular velocity vectors are labelled illustration, not measured values.

candidateSegments.teachingRole: A rotating windmill blade has one turn angle but different distances from hub.

observed.before: Windmill rotor turns behind the vehicle.
observed.action: Camera approaches as rotor continues turning.
observed.result: Hub remains attached to building; blade tips trace arcs around it.

claimLimits: Camera moves: do not measure angular or linear speed from pixel displacement.
No internal windmill motor/rigidbody implementation inferred.
Use our shared rigid-rotor model to compare exact radii, angular velocity and point speeds.
